ratings.reason: The circos grammar with explicit terminators is one of the most precisely specified constraints in the set and clearly bounds what may be generated, but it is a bioinformatics plotting DSL with little life outside that chart type.

Templates whose slots are deliberately left hidden turn a schema into a pedagogical withholding device, which is more interesting than the usual field list, though the knowledge-graph annotation pipeline is the paper's focus.

Withholding the conclusion and re-framing the explanation as a question is a genuine reframe of the over-reliance problem, and it is one of the few candidates where the constraint is tied to a measured accuracy gain.
The analogy design space does shape what gets generated, but the paper's contribution is the design space as knowledge, not an interface boundary the user encounters.
Five fixed context dimensions to record is a sensible study-instrument choice rather than an interface constraint on generation.

The incomplete S->B->A triple with the application withheld is a textbook legible instance of both patterns at once, though bio-inspired design training limits how far the specific instantiation travels.

User-defined criteria as the unit of evaluation is influential and portable, but the criteria constrain judgement of outputs rather than the generation itself, so it sits closer to the evaluation dimension than to guardrails.

CodeAid is the reference instance of reserving part of the task for the user: technically correct help with the code solution deliberately withheld, validated by a full-semester classroom deployment rather than a lab task.

Deliberately answering only part of the question so students can complete it is a small, nameable, immediately rebuildable guardrail, and it is the least obvious use of a withheld answer in the set even if the VR-classroom setting is narrow.

The uses/risks/mitigations report format is a visible constraint on what the model reports, with real stakes in model documentation, but a fixed report skeleton is the default first thing anyone would build.

Choosing not to emit the per-publisher bias verdict the pipeline could produce is editorial restraint as a design decision with real consequences, but the evidence is a sentence fragment and the second edge is generic.

Standing dietary rules declared once and enforced across later situated generations is a fair everyday-assistant instance of persistent user-authored constraints, but the mechanism is the expected one.
A prompt structure with persona, instruction and response form is standard prompt scaffolding, incidental to the UI-search contribution.

Prototyping LLM policies collaboratively is squarely on-dimension and the multi-stakeholder angle is interesting, but the coded quote is an intro definition of what a policy is and shows none of PolicyPad's actual interaction.
Feedback and goal-setting without generating text verbatim is squarely the withheld-answer contract, but by 2026 this is well-established and the quote gives no mechanism beyond the prohibition.
Questioning instead of co-authoring is the same withholding contract in a new setting; the maieutic framing is attractive but the coded evidence shows only the framing, not the interaction.

Rubrics-as-tabular-constraint with weighted user-defined criteria gives both a template and a standing rule set, but by 2026 user-authored evaluation criteria are a crowded corner and this adds refinement rather than a new move.
Expert-aligned safety templates as a guardrail on generated meditation guidance is on-dimension, yet the quote describes an agent in a pipeline rather than anything the user sees or sets.
Role play plus knowledge injection plus response format is the same generic prompt skeleton, here applied to Chinese painting ideation.
The Product/Design System/Feature/Component hierarchy is a legible structural constraint on UI generation; competent, and closer to a representation contribution than a guardrail one.
The coded quote specifies formatting of study materials for consistency across conditions, which is experimental control rather than a guardrail the interface offers the user.

Segmenting speech into a fixed structure and then eliciting the missing parts combines template and withholding for a population where the scaffold matters, but the mechanism is described only at figure-caption level.
Structured data exchanged between agents to keep story and world consistent is an internal coordination format; the user never meets the constraint.
Explanation/Action/Artifact as the fixed shape of a decision step is a clear visible template driving in-situ questioning; solid but unsurprising.
The keynote/signal/soundmark layering does structure the generated soundscape and is theory-grounded, but the paper's centre is conversational and analog refinement control, not the constraint.

Making explanations editable so the user writes rules back into the model inverts the usual XAI direction, which is the non-obvious part; the abstract-level quote states the move but not the on-screen mechanics.
Another criteria-set authoring interface; functional fragmentation is the paper's real contribution and the rule-authoring panel is supporting scaffolding.

Just-in-time weighted objectives as a general specification layer is portable and the JSON spec is concrete, but the objectives are assembled by the system rather than being a visible user-facing boundary.
Treating the system prompt as the editable policy specification and co-evolving it with a growing test set couples rule authoring to evidence, which is a real advance over authoring rules blind.
Authoring and stress-testing principle sets through persona-based exploration is a sensible extension of the constitution line, executed competently without changing what the idea does.
A model-card format for compliance evaluation is on-dimension as a declared output structure, but the contribution is an evaluation framework and the interface is barely present in the evidence.

Both edges central and the four-module prompt assembly (template plus design rules plus context rules) is spelled out well enough to rebuild, but meta-design of agent faces is a narrow payoff and rule-plus-template authoring is by now familiar.

Value-aligned personalisation with parents as reflective partners implies standing rules, but the abstract-level quote describes intent rather than any rule mechanism, so it cannot be judged on what is present.

A GUI for declaring output constraints whose satisfaction is guaranteed at decode time is a very clean instance of the dimension and trivially portable, but it is late-breaking work and constrained decoding itself was settled before this.
Ten metadata fields for museum artefacts is data schema work with essentially no transfer beyond the collection.
The case-history template segments what the model may report about a mental-health assessment, which carries real stakes, but it is a domain document format with little transfer.
A four-class object model that game generation must instantiate is spelled out precisely, but it is a conventional world-model schema in a short late-breaking paper.
Adopting an existing personalised-learning framework as the output dimensions is straightforward reuse with no interface constraint of its own.
Stored blueprints as structural templates for lyric generation is a clear enough mechanism attached to a deliberately lightweight novelty application.
The fixed acknowledge/normalise/guide response pattern is a visible behavioural constraint that matters for a vulnerable population, but it is a canned response skeleton.
Co-developing a structured language linking pedagogy to gameplay is genuinely on-dimension, but the abstract-level quote leaves the four components and their enforcement unspecified.
Constraining scoring to the original scale anchors is a real fidelity guardrail on generation and is stated precisely, but its value is confined to instrument-faithful measurement.
The quote states the guardrail rationale plainly -- a strict DSL stops the model emitting arbitrary structures -- but DSL-constrained generation was long settled by 2026.
Generating follow-ups against the STAR framework is the default move for structured interviewing and does not shape the paper's design-space contribution.
A scenario-structuring framework with LLM expansion; the constraint is a taxonomy for authors and no interface of the authors' own is visible in the evidence.

Pre-configured CTML constraints plus user-added custom requirements that the generator must respect is a clean, portable defaults-plus-overrides rule scheme; the quote shows exactly where in the flow it sits.
Structured templates plus constraint rules defining puzzle groups is on-dimension and modular, but the description stays at architecture level and the payoff is confined to word-game generation.
Prescribing user actions, system events and context as base construction units is a requirement statement, not yet a mechanism a designer could rebuild.
Forcing every segment into a question-and-answer shape is a visible, audible constraint on generated podcast structure; a sound but modest use of the pattern.

ConstitutionMaker's move -- converting an in-the-moment critique into a standing principle that governs all later generations -- is the origin point for the user-authored-rules line here, and several later candidates are variations on it.

Jamplate makes the template the interface rather than a hidden schema, which is exactly what this dimension's boundary asks for; the quote states the reframe but leaves the actual slot mechanics unshown.
Constructing competency-question patterns constrains ontology scoping sensibly, but the structure is inherited from prior work and confined to ontology engineering.

Storyboard, data model and GUI skeleton as intermediate representations do genuinely constrain what the code generator may produce, and IR-as-guardrail transfers, but they read as pipeline scaffolding more than as a declared boundary.
Tree serialisation for a transformer is a model-architecture decision, not a constraint expressed through an interface; it sits outside this dimension's stated boundary.
A controlled annotation list for labelling code segments is an analysis-pipeline convention, well short of a design move.
The four-dimension structure is a study condition in a comparison, so what is coded is an experimental manipulation rather than a deployed interface constraint.

The protocol tree that determines which questions become relevant is a real generated-output constraint and the refusal to settle analysis choices for the researcher is on-dimension, but the withheld-answer quote cites prior work instead of showing the system.
Operationalising Paul-Elder Elements of Thought into interactive slots is clear and transferable, but theory-derived reasoning scaffolds are the most-trodden version of the template pattern.

Preferences are compiled into constraint-programming predicates that are actually checked, so the guardrail binds instead of being a prompt request; the quote gives a rebuildable definition and the mechanism lifts to any domain with a solver.
A JSON schema passed with the request so XR scene generation stays parseable -- concrete and clearly stated, and also the single most ordinary version of this pattern.
An L1-L3 element classification supports hallucination measurement; the quote is about a benchmark taxonomy rather than a constraint the interface imposes on generation.
Selecting a predefined template per topic is the plainest possible instance of the pattern, stated in one line with no user-facing surface.
Requiring a JSON object with an answer and follow-up questions is boilerplate output formatting with no bearing on the paper's data-literacy claims.
A six-tuple data-fact formalisation is an internal representation for the pipeline; the constraint is real but never surfaces as something the user sets or sees.

Constraint semantics that force every LLM-generated constraint to compile into ASP is a nice two-level guardrail -- the schema constrains the constraints -- though it is buried inside a design-space-exploration contribution.
Graphologue is a landmark for interactive response representation, but the template coding is an extraction schema incidental to that contribution and reads as a neighbouring dimension's paper.

Two crisp central mechanisms -- an accumulating intent specification as the standing rule set, and a conflict check that highlights without proposing edits -- and it names a problem (rule sets going inconsistent at scale) the rest of this shortlist ignores.
The intent taxonomy grounds generation usefully, but the contribution is automated evaluation of search, with the taxonomy as internal machinery rather than a visible boundary.
Instructor-editable grading metrics extend a rubric with AI suggestions -- reasonable and useful, but the fourth instance of criteria authoring in this shortlist.
The ambiguity taxonomy becomes a disambiguation tree the user actually navigates, so the structure is interface-visible rather than internal; the move itself is standard clarification design.

Policy Projector is the dimension in its purest form: a visible Case/Concept/Policy hierarchy over model behaviour plus user-drawn regions and if-then rules that actually rewrite outputs, with both pattern edges central and quotes that show the mechanism rather than gesture at it.
Three configurable widget types bound what an in-situ prompt-driven prototype can become, which is a genuine generative constraint, though it is one component of a broader prototyping probe.

The coded quote is a prompt-engineering detail about asking GPT for CSS plus an explanation; the design probe's actual contributions lie elsewhere and this is not a constraint the designer manipulates.
Six fixed feedback sections mirroring the think-aloud process is a conventional report skeleton in an otherwise interview-driven design paper.
CounterQuill applies the no-generated-text contract to counterspeech with a plausible learning payoff, but it is the second or third instance of a move CodeAid had already established.
Interview and preference study about how users prompt for notification summaries; the coded quote reports strategies participants used, not a rule mechanism in an interface the authors built.
ratings.disqualify_reason: Interview and preference study about how users prompt for notification summaries; the coded quote reports strategies participants used, not a rule mechanism in an interface the authors built.

ratings.reason: The coded quote enumerates interface widgets for a discussion map, which shows a structured representation but not a constraint on what may be generated.
A five-section research outline panel is a form layout; on-dimension only in the weakest sense, and beside the paper's persona-simulation contribution.
A pre-derived node and edge schema constraining multimodal graph generation is on-dimension and interpretable, but it is a schema-shapes-output instance like many others here.
Prompting reports to follow a stakeholder-derived theme template is on-dimension but stated at one line, and the paper's contribution is the elicitation of the themes, not the constraint.
The instruction tuple is an internal action representation for UI automation; precise, but invisible to the user and incidental to the paper's contribution.
